Moves & help
Your moves will appear here. Try a ring or press Randomize.

Every ring turn is a legal Tetraminx move.

How to play & keyboard shortcuts

Select a layer to highlight its moving pieces.

Make each of the four faces a single color. Choose a letter under Main layers, then press a direction button. You can also drag any ring and release for one 120° turn.

Uppercase U L R B turn the upper, left, right and back layers. The Tetraminx is the tipless relative of the Pyraminx: its four truncated corners have dark triangular caps. These labels stay attached to the puzzle as you change your view. Drag the 3D puzzle to look around; scroll or pinch to zoom. Click a vertex letter to select its main layer. “View selected axis” looks straight down that vertex.

The 24 single-color dots form four face-color clusters in the solved state. Shared edge stickers sit at the intersections of their two rotation rings. A move turns three edges and one vertex piece. Selecting an axis highlights its nine affected stickers; the dark tip caps do not carry colors.

The selected rings and arrows stay bright while the other tracks fade into the background. “Show all rings” reveals the surrounding paths; “Focus selected rings” restores the quieter view. Moving dots follow their ring to the next sticker position, and the map stays fixed as you select or turn an axis.

Use ← and → for the selected ring. Keys U, L, R, B turn main layers; hold Shift to reverse. A prime (′) means counterclockwise looking from the selected vertex toward the puzzle’s center. Each move is 120°. Arrow buttons turn the selected ring clockwise or counterclockwise as it appears here. With the 3D view focused, arrow keys rotate the camera and +/− zoom.

Randomize continues from the current position and applies 20 legal layer turns, using a fresh seed each time. Auto solve opens the Constrained Solver and works from the current arrangement, pausing between stages and highlighting solved nodes that later stages protect. It does not need recorded moves or promise the shortest solution; difficult states may reach the computation limit. Your puzzle state stays in this browser tab.
